candidate_relations.reason: While Bednar tumor shares CD34 positivity and spindled cells, it is a malignant neoplasm (DFSP variant) with storiform architecture and S100/SOX10-positive melanocytic cells. The lesion here is S100/SOX10/HMB45/Melan-A negative, lacks mitoses, and shows hemosiderin-laden fibrolipomatous histology inconsistent with Bednar tumor.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Bednar tumor is a pigmented variant of DFSP, a malignant neoplasm; HFLT is a distinct benign entity

candidate_relations.reason: DFSP is CD34-positive but is a malignant neoplasm with storiform pattern and no significant adipose or hemosiderin component. The histology here shows mature adipose tissue, extensive pigment deposition, and no mitoses, which is characteristic of HFLT rather than DFSP.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: DFSP is a malignant fibroblastic tumor; HFLT is a distinct benign fibrolipomatous lesion

candidate_relations.reason: Hemosiderotic Fibrohistiocytic Lipoma (also called hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor) is the same entity: a benign CD34-positive lesion with mixed fibrous and adipose tissue, hemosiderin pigment deposition, spindled/epithelioid cells without mitoses, and mixed inflammatory infiltrate, arising in acral soft tissue after trauma. All histologic, immunohistochemical, and clinical features match.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hemosiderotic Fibrohistiocytic Lipoma is an accepted synonym for HFLT
